<!-- Generated by tools/docgen from doc comments. Do not edit: run scripts/docs.sh. -->

```odin
import clip "fire:clip"
```

Clips: musical content that plays on the clock's timelines.

A `Midi_Clip` holds notes (with per-note expression) and controller events,
in beats. It is immutable once built: the app keeps its own editable model
and builds a new clip after each edit, then hands it to the players, which
swap it in at their next block. Clips are reference counted, so one clip can
play in several places.

```odin
b: clip.Midi_Builder
clip.midi_builder_init(&b, length = 4)
n := clip.add_note(&b, start = 0, length = 1, key = 60, velocity = 0.8)
clip.add_expression(&b, n, at = 0.5, kind = .Tuning, value = 1) // bend up a semitone
clip.add_controller(&b, at = 2, bytes = {0xB0, 74, 100})        // CC 74
c, _ := clip.midi_build(&b)
clip.midi_builder_destroy(&b)

node, player := clip.midi_player_create({timeline = song})
clip.midi_player_set(player, c, {loop = true}) // loops the clip from the timeline's beat 0
clip.midi_clip_release(c)                     // the player keeps its own reference
```

Audio clips (`Audio_Clip`, `audio_player_create`) play regions of files
through `fire:stream`, at their own speed or following the tempo. See
/guides/clips/ for placing clips in arrangements and launchers.

## Constants

### DECLICK_FRAMES

```odin
DECLICK_FRAMES :: 128
```

Frames over which starts fade in and stops and jumps crossfade.

## Types

### Audio_Mode

```odin
Audio_Mode :: enum u8 {
	Original,
	Repitch,
	Stretch,
}
```

How an audio clip relates to tempo.

| Value | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `Original` | plays at the file's own speed whatever the tempo (one-shots, dialogue, field recordings) |
| `Repitch` | follows tempo by playing faster or slower, so pitch moves with it (turntable-style) |
| `Stretch` | follows tempo at the original pitch (time-stretching; the player needs a `Stretcher_VTable`) |

### Audio_Clip_Settings

```odin
Audio_Clip_Settings :: struct {
	start: i64,
	end: i64,
	loop_start: i64,
	loop_end: i64,
	bpm: f64,
	mode: Audio_Mode,
	gain: f32,
	fade_in: f64,
	fade_out: f64,
}
```

How to make an audio clip from a source. Positions are in the source's
frames.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `start` | first frame used |
| `end` | one past the last frame used; 0 = the end of the file |
| `loop_start` | part repeated by a looping placement; 0 and 0 = all of start..end |
| `loop_end` |  |
| `bpm` | the material's tempo, to place it in beats; needed by Repitch and Stretch |
| `mode` |  |
| `gain` | linear; 0 is taken as 1 |
| `fade_in` | seconds, at the clip's start; negative = none, 0 = 5 ms |
| `fade_out` | seconds, at the clip's end; negative = none, 0 = 5 ms |

### Audio_Clip

```odin
Audio_Clip :: struct {
	source: ^stream.Source,
	using settings: Audio_Clip_Settings,
	sample_rate: f64,
	channels: int,
	refs: int,
	allocator: mem.Allocator,
}
```

An immutable audio clip: a region of a streamed or in-memory source and
how to play it. Create with `audio_clip_create`; release with
`audio_clip_release`. Read its fields freely, never change them.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `source` |  |
| `settings` | with `end`, the loop and the fades resolved |
| `sample_rate` | the source's |
| `channels` |  |
| `refs` | control thread |
| `allocator` |  |

```odin
Audio_Player_Settings :: struct {

	channels: int,
	quality: dsp.Resampler_Quality,
	max_speed: f64,

}
```

Settings for `audio_player_create`. Start from `default_audio_player_settings`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `timeline` |  |
| `streamer` | reads the clips' sources |
| `channels` | the node's output channels |
| `quality` | for rate conversion and repitching |

### Audio_Player

```odin
Audio_Player :: struct {...}
```

Plays an `Audio_Clip` on a timeline, as a graph node with `channels`
audio outputs (no inputs). Uses the same `Placement`s as MIDI clips.

- Converts the source's sample rate to the device's, and in `.Repitch`
  mode follows the tempo (and timeline rate) by playing faster or slower.
  A small continuous correction keeps it locked to the timeline through
  tempo changes, with no seeking.
- Loops are seamless: the resampler is fed audio that already wraps at
  the loop points.
- Never clicks: starts fade in, and stops and jumps crossfade over
  `DECLICK_FRAMES`.
- Reads through `fire:stream`: jumps to the clip start, its loop start and
  the placement's offset are instant; others are silent until the disk
  delivers (see `audio_player_ready`).

Mono sources play on every output; with a mono output, channels are
averaged; otherwise channel c plays on output c. Fields are internal.

### Note

```odin
Note :: struct {

}
```

One note of a clip.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `start` | from the clip's start |
| `length` | > 0 |
| `key` | 0..127 |
| `channel` | 0..15 |
| `velocity` | 0..1 |
| `release` | release velocity, 0..1 |
| `expression` | range [first, first + count) in `Midi_Clip.expression` |

### Controller

```odin
Controller :: struct {
	at: timebase.Beats,

```

A MIDI 1.0 channel message (control change, pitch bend, channel or key

### Midi_Clip

```odin
Midi_Clip :: struct {
	length: timebase.Beats,
	loop_start: timebase.Beats,
	loop_end: timebase.Beats,
	notes: []Note,
	expression: []Expression_Point,
	controllers: []Controller,
	refs: int,
	allocator: mem.Allocator,
}
```

An immutable MIDI clip. Build with `Midi_Builder`; read its fields freely
but never change them (players read them on the audio thread). Release
with `midi_clip_release`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `length` | the clip's length in beats |
| `loop_start` | the part repeated when a placement loops |
| `loop_end` |  |
| `notes` | sorted by start, then key |
| `expression` | grouped by note, each group sorted by `at` |
| `controllers` | sorted by `at` |
| `refs` | control thread |
| `allocator` |  |

### Midi_Builder

```odin
Midi_Builder :: struct {
	length: timebase.Beats,
	loop_start: timebase.Beats,
	loop_end: timebase.Beats,
	notes: [dynamic]Note,
	expression: [dynamic]Builder_Expression,
	controllers: [dynamic]Controller,
}
```

Collects notes and events for a clip. Control thread.

### Placement

```odin
Placement :: struct {
	at: timebase.Beats,
	length: timebase.Beats,
	offset: timebase.Beats,
	loop: bool,
}
```

Where a clip sits on its timeline.

- Launcher: `{loop = true}`: the clip starts at the timeline's beat 0 and
  repeats its loop for as long as the timeline plays.
- Arrangement: `{at = 32, length = 16, offset = 4}`: on the timeline from
  beat 32 for 16 beats, starting 4 beats into the clip; add `loop` to
  repeat the clip's loop within those 16 beats.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `at` | timeline position where playback of the clip begins |
| `length` | how long it plays on the timeline; 0 = no end |
| `offset` | clip position played at `at` |
| `loop` | after reaching the clip's loop end, repeat loop_start..loop_end |

### Midi_Player_Settings

```odin
Midi_Player_Settings :: struct {
	timeline: core.Timeline_Id,
	max_notes: int,
	max_events: int,
}
```

Settings for `midi_player_create`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `timeline` | the timeline it follows |
| `max_notes` | notes sounding at once; 0 = 256 (more are dropped and counted) |
| `max_events` | events per process call; 0 = 1024 (more are dropped and counted) |

### Midi_Player

```odin
Midi_Player :: struct {...}
```

Plays a `Midi_Clip` on a timeline as note and controller events. It is a
graph node (0 audio channels): event-connect it to an instrument.

Notes land on their exact frame. On a stop, every sounding note ends; on a
start, jump, loop wrap or entry into the clip, notes already in progress
start at once with what remains of them ("chasing"). Notes are cut at the
clip's loop end and at the end of the placement. Each note gets its own
`core.Note_Id`, which its expression events and note-off carry.

Fields are internal.

### Stretcher_VTable

```odin
Stretcher_VTable :: struct {
	create: proc(channels: int, sample_rate: f64, max_rate: f64) -> rawptr,
	destroy: proc(s: rawptr),
	input_latency: proc(s: rawptr) -> int,
	output_latency: proc(s: rawptr) -> int,
	output_seek: proc "contextless"(s: rawptr, input: [][]f32, frames: int),
	process: proc "contextless"(s: rawptr, input: [][]f32, in_frames: int, output: [][]f32, out_frames: int),
}
```

A time-stretcher for `.Stretch` audio clips: changes duration, not pitch.
Fire Engine's clips don't depend on any particular one; `fire:stretch`
provides Signalsmith Stretch, and you can supply your own. Give it to the
player in `Audio_Player_Settings.stretcher`.

The player feeds it audio at the device's sample rate and keeps it in
sync with this model: after `output_seek` with input starting at
position P, the next output is P; from then on, the position heard is
the input fed so far, minus `input_latency`, minus the playback rate
(input per output frame) times `output_latency`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `create` | Control thread. A stretcher for `channels` channels at `sample_rate`, ready for rates up to `max_rate` (input frames per output frame). After this, no other proc may allocate. nil on failure. |
| `destroy` | Control thread. |
| `input_latency` | Frames of input ahead of the position being processed. |
| `output_latency` | Frames by which output trails the position being processed. |
| `output_seek` | [rt] Start over so that the next output begins at input frame 0; `frames` = input_latency + rate × output_latency. |
| `process` | [rt] Consume `in_frames` frames and produce `out_frames`; their ratio is the playback rate. |

## Procedures

### audio_clip_create

```odin
audio_clip_create :: proc(src: ^stream.Source, settings: Audio_Clip_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (^Audio_Clip, core.Error)
```

Control thread. Makes a clip on `src` (which it keeps a reference to).
Fails with `.Invalid_Argument` for an empty or out-of-range region or
loop, or a Repitch or Stretch clip without a `bpm`.

### audio_clip_retain

```odin
audio_clip_retain :: proc(c: ^Audio_Clip)
```

Control thread. Adds a reference.

### audio_clip_release

```odin
audio_clip_release :: proc(c: ^Audio_Clip)
```

Control thread. Drops a reference; the clip (and its hold on the source)
goes with the last one.

### audio_clip_beats

```odin
audio_clip_beats :: proc "contextless"(c: ^Audio_Clip) -> timebase.Beats
```

The clip's length in beats at its `bpm` (0 without one).

### default_audio_player_settings

```odin
default_audio_player_settings :: proc(timeline: core.Timeline_Id, streamer: ^stream.Streamer) -> Audio_Player_Settings
```

Stereo out, Medium resampling, up to 4× speed.

### audio_player_create

```odin
audio_player_create :: proc(settings: Audio_Player_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (node: core.Node, player: ^Audio_Player)
```

Control thread. Creates a player node and a handle for controlling it;
the handle stays valid until the graph destroys the node. Add it with
`graph.add_node(g, node, 0, settings.channels)`.

### audio_player_set

```odin
audio_player_set :: proc(p: ^Audio_Player, clip: ^Audio_Clip, placement: Placement) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Plays `clip` (nil: nothing) placed as `placement`, from
the player's next block; the switch crossfades. Allocates the clip's
stream (with cues at the clip's start, its loop start and the placement's
start), resampler and (for `.Stretch`) stretcher now. Keeps its own
reference to the clip. A `.Stretch` clip needs `settings.stretcher`
(`.Unsupported` otherwise) and a prepared node (`.Invalid_State`: add it
to the graph first).

### audio_player_ready

```odin
audio_player_ready :: proc(p: ^Audio_Player) -> bool
```

Control thread. Whether the clip given to the last `audio_player_set` can
start without a dropout (its stream's start and cues are buffered). Poll
it before a quantized launch.

### midi_builder_init

```odin
midi_builder_init :: proc(b: ^Midi_Builder, length: timebase.Beats, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator)
```

Starts a clip of `length` beats, looping over all of it.

### midi_builder_destroy

```odin
midi_builder_destroy :: proc(b: ^Midi_Builder)
```

Frees the builder (not the clips built from it).

### add_note

```odin
add_note :: proc(b: ^Midi_Builder, start: timebase.Beats, length: timebase.Beats, key: u8, velocity: f32, channel: u8 = 0, release: f32 = 0.5) -> int
```

Adds a note; returns its index for `add_expression`. Notes may be added in
any order.

### add_expression

```odin
add_expression :: proc(b: ^Midi_Builder, note: int, at: timebase.Beats, kind: core.Note_Expression_Kind, value: f64)
```

Adds an expression change to note `note`, `at` beats after it starts.

### add_controller

```odin
add_controller :: proc(b: ^Midi_Builder, at: timebase.Beats, bytes: [3]u8)
```

Adds a channel message at `at` (`bytes[0]` is the status byte).

### set_loop

```odin
set_loop :: proc(b: ^Midi_Builder, start: timebase.Beats, end: timebase.Beats)
```

Sets the part a looping placement repeats (default: the whole clip).

### midi_build

```odin
midi_build :: proc(b: ^Midi_Builder, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (c: ^Midi_Clip, err: core.Error)
```

Makes an immutable clip from the builder's contents, with one reference
held by the caller. The builder can keep being edited and built again.

### midi_clip_retain

```odin
midi_clip_retain :: proc(c: ^Midi_Clip)
```

Control thread. Adds a reference (one per place the clip is kept).

### midi_clip_release

```odin
midi_clip_release :: proc(c: ^Midi_Clip)
```

Control thread. Drops a reference; the clip is freed with the last one.

### midi_player_create

```odin
midi_player_create :: proc(settings: Midi_Player_Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (node: core.Node, player: ^Midi_Player)
```

Control thread. Creates a player node and a handle for controlling it.
Give the node to the graph (`graph.add_node(g, node, 0, 0)`); the handle
stays valid until the graph destroys the node.

### midi_player_set

```odin
midi_player_set :: proc(p: ^Midi_Player, clip: ^Midi_Clip, placement: Placement) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Plays `clip` (nil: nothing) placed as `placement`, from
the player's next block. The player keeps its own reference to the clip.
Notes already sounding finish normally.

### midi_player_dropped

```odin
midi_player_dropped :: proc "contextless"(p: ^Midi_Player) -> u64
```

Any thread. Notes or events dropped because `max_notes` or `max_events`
was full.

### midi_file_read

```odin
midi_file_read :: proc(path: string, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (mf: Midi_File, err: File_Error)
```

Reads a type 0 or 1 Standard MIDI File. Each track with notes or
controllers becomes a clip (all channels kept, notes paired in order),
as long as the longest track, rounded up to a whole bar. Tempo and time
signature changes go into `tempo_map`. SysEx and other meta events are
skipped.

### midi_file_parse

```odin
midi_file_parse :: proc(data: []u8, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (mf: Midi_File, err: File_Error)
```

Like `midi_file_read`, from bytes already in memory.

### midi_file_destroy

```odin
midi_file_destroy :: proc(mf: ^Midi_File)
```

Frees what `midi_file_read` returned, releasing its clips (clips retained
elsewhere live on).

### midi_file_write

```odin
midi_file_write :: proc(path: string, tracks: []Midi_File_Track, tempo_map: ^timebase.Tempo_Map = nil, ppq: int = 960) -> File_Error
```

Writes a type 1 Standard MIDI File: a conductor track with the tempo
map's tempos and time signatures (ramps written as steps every eighth
note; nil: 120 BPM in 4/4), then one track per clip with its name, notes
and controllers. Per-note expression has no MIDI 1.0 form and is not
written. Times are rounded to `ppq` ticks per quarter note.
